sentences.text: This is the second application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail filed by the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.201/2023 dated 23.5.2023 registered at Police Station Gadh, Rewa, district Rewa, for the offences punishable under Sections 409 and 420/34 of IPC and Section 3/7 of Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and h a s been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is a permanent resident of district Rewa and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.
The applicant is willing and ready to abide by all the directions and conditions to be imposed by this Court.
Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that the trial would take considerable time.

Therefore, prayer has Santosh Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186380551/
1 been made to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State had opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

This repeat anticipatory bail application has been primarily opposed by the State on the ground that there can be no substantial change in circumstances while considering the repeat anticipatory bail application, hence it should be dismissed for the simple reason that the first anticipatory bail application has already been dismissed on merits under M.Cr.C. No.2636/2023.

For this, the learned counsel for the applicant has relied on the decision of the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Haneef Khan v. State of M.P. 2021 SCC Online MP 5947 and Imratlal Vishwakarma and others v. State of M.P. 1996 SCC Online M.P. 59 in which it has been held that repeat application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. may be entertained if incorrect facts were available before the Court while deciding the earlier application.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further reliance has also been placed on citation of Yuvraj Gaud v. State of M.P. and another 2004 SCC Online M.P. 203 wherein again it has been held that repeat application for anticipatory bail may be allowed.

entities.text: Yuvraj Gaud v. State of M.P. and another 2004 SCC Online M.P. 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the objections raised by the State about the maintainability of this repeat anticipatory bail application cannot be accepted.
This repeat anticipatory bail application has been argued on the ground that applicant is innocent and he is not involved in any diversion or misappropriation of food grains.

It has also been argued that applicant is ready to deposit the amount of allegedly misappropriated food grain though under protest and for this, the citation of Ramesh Kumar v. The State of NCT of Delhi 2023 LiveLaw (SC)
496 has been relied upon wherein it has been observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that willingness of accused to deposit money may be considered in cases involving public money and anticipatory bail can be granted under Section 438 Cr.P.C.

entities.text:
Ramesh Kumar v. The State of NCT of Delhi 2023 LiveLaw (SC)
496
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Incidentally, this proposal regarding depositing the amount under protest was not there when the first anticipatory application was considered.

In the light of these changed circumstances arisen from the proposal made by the applicant, this repeat bail application is allowed and it is directed that on payment of Rs.5,28,935/- before the concerned authority of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department and subject to its verification by the arresting authority concerned,
the applicant in the event of arrest in the aforesaid crime, shall be released on bail on furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer) for his regular appearance before the Police/Arresting Officer during the investigation or before the Court during trial, as the case may be.

It is directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 438(2) of Cr.P.C., failing which this order shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
